_note: Sources for Form 2 English (Batches E2-1, E2-2 and E2-3, Terms 1–3). Reading texts, dialogues and item banks are written for this app; a teacher must check them.

reading-texts.ref: Reading texts, interviews and dialogues written for this app on the themes of the Form 2 progression sheet (2026-27)
reading-texts.supports: Comprehension answers are taken from the app's own texts; the language of travel, the clinic, the telephone and polite conversation.
reading-texts.checked: Authored for this app, not externally sourced: please check that the texts and answers suit Form Two.

vocabulary.ref: Standard English word meanings (British usage, as in Cameroonian schools), compare a learner's dictionary such as the Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary
vocabulary.supports: Meanings and uses of the topic words (travel, dental care, health, weather, telephone and shopping, humanitarian work, synonyms, word formation).
vocabulary.checked: Not externally sourced: please check each meaning against the textbook.

grammar-tenses.ref: Standard descriptions of English tenses and modals (e.g. Swan, Practical English Usage)
grammar-tenses.supports: Form and use of the Simple Present, Present Continuous, Simple Past, Present Perfect, Past Perfect and Simple Future; state verbs; adverbs of frequency; modals and polite requests.
grammar-tenses.checked: Verb forms are computed by the English library (tested on known answers, TR-E01 to TR-E04); explanations are authored.

spelling-rules.ref: English spelling rules for adding endings (British spelling)
spelling-rules.supports: Drop silent e before -ing; double a final consonant after one short stressed vowel (and l in British English); consonant + y → i; vowel + y keeps y.
spelling-rules.checked: Computed by the English library (ing, past, thirdPerson, plural), tested on known answers.

writing-skills.ref: Paragraph and composition writing as taught in Cameroonian secondary schools: topic sentence, supporting details, sequence words, closing sentence
writing-skills.supports: The self-check lists and model answers of the writing lessons.
writing-skills.checked: Authored, not externally sourced: please check that the model answers are at Form Two level.

health-facts.ref: WHO fact sheets on cholera, malaria and COVID-19 (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets); Cameroon Ministry of Public Health prevention messages
health-facts.supports: Cholera spreads through contaminated water and food and is treated with oral rehydration salts; malaria is carried by mosquitoes (not passed from person to person) and prevented with nets; COVID-19 spreads through droplets; handwashing with soap removes germs; which specialist treats which part of the body.
health-facts.checked: General facts from the WHO fact sheets, from memory (the pages were not opened in this session): please check, especially the health statements.

cameroon-holidays.ref: Public holidays of Cameroon (law on public holidays; government calendar): New Year's Day 1 January, Youth Day 11 February, Labour Day 1 May, National Day 20 May, Assumption Day 15 August, Christmas Day 25 December; Good Friday, Ascension Day, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha on moving dates
cameroon-holidays.supports: The dates and meanings of the holidays in Lesson 29.
cameroon-holidays.checked: From general knowledge, not opened in this session: please check the list and the meanings (National Day: unity; Youth Day: young people).

word-formation.ref: English prefixes and suffixes (e.g. Swan, Practical English Usage; a learner's dictionary)
word-formation.supports: un-, dis-, im-, in-, re-, mis-; -ion, -ment, -ness, -dom, -er; -ful, -less, -al; -ly; spelling changes (y → i, dropped e).
word-formation.checked: Not externally sourced: please check against the textbook.

culture-film.ref: Festivals of Cameroon (Ngondo of the Sawa, Ngouon of the Bamoun, Lela of Bali Nyonga, Nyem-Nyem), music styles (makossa, bikutsi, bend skin, njang, assiko), national languages, the Cameroon film industry (“Collywood”, the Écrans Noirs festival in Yaoundé), Manu Dibango (born Douala 1933, “Soul Makossa” 1972, died 2020)
culture-film.supports: The original reading texts and dialogues of rows 77, 81, 85, 89, 93, 94; Adah Mbeng and Ngum Rose are model (invented) artists, labelled as such.
culture-film.checked: General knowledge, not opened in this session: please check the festival, music and film facts and the Manu Dibango dates.
